units.spec:
A pure ADAPTIVE MUSIC SEQUENCER. It emits bars of note events; something else plays them. Import `rng` is NOT needed - an rng object is passed in.
Export `SCALES` = { minorPent: [0,3,5,7,10], dorian: [0,2,3,5,7,9,10], phrygian: [0,1,3,5,7,8,10] } (semitone offsets, each starting at 0). Export `noteHz(midi)` = 440 * 2^((midi-69)/12).
Export `createScore(rng)` -> { root: rng.int(36,48), scaleName: rng.pick(Object.keys(SCALES)), bpm: rng.int(100,150), intensity: 0, bar: 0, boss: false, plus any motif/seed data you like (e.g. an 8-step motif of scale degrees drawn from rng) }. Deterministic per rng seed.
Export `setIntensity(score, v)`: score.intensity = clamp(v, 0, 1) (mutates).
Export `nextBar(score, rng)` -> { events, barIndex, beatSec: 60/bpm }, and increments score.bar (barIndex is the value BEFORE incrementing). `events` is an array of { voice, t, dur, gain, midi? } where voice is one of kick, snare, hat, bass, lead, pad; t is the beat offset in [0,4) within a 4/4 bar; dur > 0 (beats); gain in (0,1]; bass/lead/pad carry an integer `midi`, drums do not.
Musical rules the tests check: (1) EVERY pitched note is in key: ((midi - root) mod 12) must be an element of SCALES[scaleName] - build notes as root + scale[degree % len] + 12*octave. (2) intensity 0: emit a `pad` (a long note, dur 4, at root + 12 or so) and at most sparse `bass`; NO kick, NO snare, NO lead. (3) intensity >= 0.5: a `kick` exactly at t=0 of every bar (plus more if you like), and `hat`s; intensity 1: kick and hat every bar, and `lead` notes appear across a few bars. (4) event count per bar must strictly rise with intensity (0 < 0.5 < 1) - add voices and subdivisions as it rises. (5) all `bass` midi values are strictly BELOW all `lead` midi values (bass in octave 0-1 above root, lead in octave 2+). (6) bars must VARY: over 8 bars at intensity 0.8 the set of (lead/bass midi @ t) patterns must not all be identical - use the motif index shifted by bar and use rng.chance() for rests/ornaments. (7) if score.boss is true: add a low `pad` at or below root (midi <= root) and DOUBLE the hat density (e.g. 16ths instead of 8ths). Deterministic for the same score state + rng seed.

A pooled particle SIMULATION (no rendering). Export `PRESETS`: an object with keys hit, crit, kill, explosion, muzzle, dash, pickup, burn, spark - each { count, life, speed, size, color (a number like 0xffd080), gravity, drag, spread, and optionally bounce }. Constraints tests check: crit.count > hit.count; kill.count > hit.count; explosion.count > kill.count; every count/life/speed/size > 0. Suggested: hit 6/0.35s/5, crit 14, kill 24, explosion 60, muzzle 5, dash 12, pickup 20, burn 3, spark 10.
Export `createPool(capacity)` -> { capacity, alive: 0, px, py, pz, vx, vy, vz, life, maxLife, size (all Float32Array(capacity)), color (Uint32Array(capacity)), and any bookkeeping you need e.g. a per-particle preset ref }.
Export `emit(pool, preset, pos, dir, rng)` -> number emitted. count = floor(preset.count); if 0 return 0. If adding count would exceed capacity, RECYCLE the OLDEST particles (lowest remaining life) to make room; never exceed capacity. For each new particle: position = pos exactly; velocity = a random unit direction (uniform on the sphere via rng.next()) times preset.speed*(0.5+rng.next()); if `dir` is given (a unit vector), bias the direction toward it (blend then renormalise) so the mean velocity along dir is positive; life = preset.life*(0.7+0.6*rng.next()) and maxLife = life; size = preset.size*(0.7+0.6*rng.next()); color = preset.color. Deterministic per rng seed.
Export `step(pool, dt, gravity)` -> pool.alive after. For each live particle: g = preset.gravity if the preset has one else the `gravity` argument; vy -= g*dt; if preset.drag > 0 apply EXPONENTIAL drag: v *= Math.exp(-drag*dt) (never reaches zero or flips sign); then p += v*dt; if preset.bounce and py < 0: py = 0, vy = -vy*bounce, vx and vz *= 0.8; life -= dt; remove particles with life <= 0 by swap-with-last so the live ones stay packed in [0, alive) with no gaps. Empty pool: return 0.

Trauma-based camera shake. Export `createShake(opts={})` -> { trauma: 0, t: 0, decay: opts.decay ?? 1.2, maxOffset: opts.maxOffset ?? 0.12, maxRoll: opts.maxRoll ?? 0.06, freq: opts.freq ?? 18 }. Export `addTrauma(s, amount)`: if amount > 0, s.trauma = min(1, s.trauma + amount); non-positive amounts are ignored. Export `stepShake(s, dt)`: s.t += dt; s.trauma = max(0, s.trauma - s.decay*dt) (linear decay). Export `sampleShake(s, rng)` -> { x, y, roll } and MUST NOT mutate s. If trauma <= 0 return exactly { x: 0, y: 0, roll: 0 }. Otherwise magnitude m = trauma*trauma (SQUARED - 0.5 trauma gives ~1/4 the shake of 1.0). Offsets come from SMOOTH noise in [-1,1] evaluated at t*freq - e.g. a sum of a few sines with incommensurate frequencies and different phase offsets per axis (do NOT use rng.next() per sample: that is white noise and consecutive frames would jump wildly; the test requires the frame-to-frame change in x at dt=0.008 to stay under 0.5 when maxOffset is 1). x = noise0*m*maxOffset, y = noise1*m*maxOffset, roll = noise2*m*maxRoll; each noise must produce both signs and reach at least ~0.3 magnitude over time. Results are bounded by maxOffset/maxRoll.

Floating damage numbers as a pool + a pure world->screen projection. Export `createNumbers(capacity)` -> { capacity, items: [] }. Export `pushNumber(n, { value, x, y, z, kind = "hit", targetId = null })`. Kinds: hit { life 0.7, scale 1.0, vy 1.6 }, crit { life 0.9, scale 1.6, vy 2.2 }, heal { life 0.8, scale 1.0, vy 1.4 }, dot { life 0.5, scale 0.8, vy 1.2 } - crit must have larger scale than hit and life >= hit's. Each entry: { value, text, x, y, z, kind, targetId, age: 0, life, scale, vy, alpha: 1 }. text = Math.max(1, Math.round(value)) as a string, prefixed with "+" for kind heal (so 0.4 -> "1", 12.6 -> "13", heal 5 -> "+5"). MERGING: if targetId is not null and an existing entry has the SAME targetId AND SAME kind AND age <= 0.12, then add value into it, recompute text, reset its age to 0, update its position, and do NOT add a new entry. Different kind (e.g. crit vs hit) never merges. If items.length >= capacity, remove the OLDEST (first) before pushing.
Export `stepNumbers(n, dt)` -> items.length after: for each entry age += dt, y += vy*dt, alpha = 1 while age/life < 0.6 then fades linearly to 0 at age == life; remove entries with age >= life.
Export `projectToScreen(p, m, w, h)` where m is a COLUMN-MAJOR 4x4 array (three.js convention: m[0],m[4],m[8],m[12] is the first row): clip = m * [p.x,p.y,p.z,1]; if clip.w <= 0 return { x: 0, y: 0, visible: false }; ndc = clip/w; visible = every ndc component in [-1,1]; return { x: (ndc.x+1)/2*w, y: (1-ndc.y)/2*h, visible } - screen y grows DOWNWARD so ndc y=+1 is the top (y=0).

Room hazards as pure state machines. Export `HAZARD_DEFS` with keys lava_floor, turrets, mines, acid_pools, collapsing, each { name, desc }.
Export `spawnHazards(rng, tag, arena, floor)` -> array. arena = { halfW, halfD, blocks }. If tag is null/unknown return []. d = max(0, floor-1). Count: lava 3-5, turrets 2-3, mines 5-8, acid 3-4, collapsing 6-9 (rng.int) plus floor(d/2) more. Positions: rng.int in x in [-halfW+2, halfW-2], z in [-halfD+2, halfD-2], REJECTING any within 5 of the player spawn at (0, halfD-4) (retry; cap attempts). Every hazard: { id (unique string), kind (= tag), x, z, radius > 0 } plus per kind - lava_floor: radius 2-3.5, dps 12+3d; acid_pools: radius 2-3, dps 8+2d, slow 0.4; turrets: radius 0.7, range 16, cd 1.5, cdMax 1.6, damage 10+2d, y 1.2; mines: radius 1.4, armed true, damage 35+5d, blast 3.5; collapsing: radius 1.8, state "solid", timer 1.2, dps 20. Deterministic per rng.
Export `stepHazards(hazards, dt, player, rng)` -> { hazards, events } - a NEW array of NEW hazard objects; never mutate the input. player = { x, y, z }. `inside` = distance in xz <= radius. lava: if inside push { type: "damage", amount: dps*dt, source: id }. acid: same damage plus { type: "slow", amount: slow, source: id }. mines: if armed and inside push { type: "explode", x, z, radius: blast, damage, source: id } and DROP the mine from the returned list (it is gone; it never explodes twice); else keep it. turrets: cd -= dt; if xz distance <= range and cd <= 0: push { type: "shoot", x, y, z, dir: unit vector from turret (x,y,z) toward player, damage, speed: 22, source: id } and set cd = cdMax; out of range: never shoot. collapsing: state solid -> "cracking" the first tick the player is inside; while cracking, timer -= dt regardless of where the player is (leaving does NOT reset it); when timer <= 0 state = "hole"; a hole deals { type: "damage", amount: dps*dt } while the player is inside.

Vector maths for the flashy items; all vectors are plain {x,y,z}; never mutate inputs.
`chainTargets(enemies, originId, count, range)`: enemies are [{ id, x, y, z }]. Starting from the enemy with id originId, repeatedly pick the NEAREST not-yet-used enemy within `range` of the PREVIOUS link (not of the origin), up to `count` links; return the array of chosen enemy objects in order. Never include the origin; never repeat; return [] if originId is unknown or count <= 0.
`singularityPull(center, pos, radius, strength, dt)`: if the distance from pos to center is 0 or > radius return {x:0,y:0,z:0}; else return a vector pointing from pos TOWARD center with length strength * falloff * dt where falloff = min(4, 1 / max(0.25, dist/radius)) - stronger nearer the centre, but capped so it never blows up. Scales linearly with dt.
`ricochetDir(dir, normal)`: normalise both; return the unit reflection d - 2*(d.n)*n. Head-on (dir = -normal) sends it straight back.
`explosionVictims(center, radius, enemies, excludeId = null)`: for each enemy (skipping excludeId) within radius return { id, dist, falloff } with falloff = 1 at the centre decreasing linearly to 0.25 at the edge (e.g. 1 - dist/radius*0.75); order by input order.
`homingSteer(dir, pos, target, maxTurn)`: d = normalise(dir); if maxTurn <= 0 return d unchanged; want = normalise(target - pos); ang = acos(clamp(d.want)); if ang <= maxTurn return want (snap on); else rotate d toward want by exactly maxTurn radians (slerp in their plane) and return the unit result.

The run state machine. Import: `rng` from "core/rng.js"; `ITEM_BY_ID` from "core/items.js"; `computeStats, BASE_STATS` from "core/stats.js"; `draftRewards` from "core/draft.js"; `generateFloor` from "core/floor.js"; `rollWeapon` from "core/weapons.js"; `scoreRun` from "core/score.js". Every exported function returns a NEW run object and never mutates its input. Phases: "floor_start" | "room" | "reward" | "door" | "boss" | "extracted" | "dead". Calling a transition in the wrong phase THROWS; any transition on an ended run (dead/extracted) THROWS.

A run object has: seed, floor (starts 1), phase, roomIndex, held (array of item ids), weapon, stats (from computeStats(BASE_STATS, held item objects)), maxHp (= stats.maxHp), hp, cursesEnabled, kills, roomsCleared, banked (0), finalScore (0), currentFloor (null or a floor object), draft (array of items), secondWindUsedFloor (0), loopUsed (false), depthReached (1).

Exports:
- newRun(seed, opts={}): phase floor_start, floor 1, held [], hp = maxHp, cursesEnabled = !!opts.cursesEnabled, weapon = rollWeapon(rng(seed).fork("weapon"), opts.startingWeapon ?? "sidearm", 1). Deterministic per seed.
- startFloor(run): needs floor_start. currentFloor = generateFloor(rng(run.seed).fork(`floor${run.floor}`), run.floor, run); phase room; roomIndex 0; depthReached = max(depthReached, floor).
- enterRoom(run): returns run unchanged (reserved).
- clearRoom(run, {kills=0}): needs room. kills += kills; roomsCleared += 1; draft = draftRewards(rng(run.seed).fork(`draft${floor}-${roomIndex}`), run); phase reward.
- takeReward(run, index): needs reward. If index is null/undefined: take nothing. Else index must be an integer in [0, draft.length) or THROW; push draft[index].id onto held, recompute stats/maxHp via computeStats, and RAISE hp by however much maxHp increased (hp = min(maxHp, hp + (newMax - oldMax))). Clear draft. Phase = "boss" if roomIndex >= 4 else "door".
- chooseDoor(run, index): needs door. index must be a valid index into currentFloor.rooms[roomIndex].doors or THROW. roomIndex += 1; phase room.
- beatBoss(run): needs boss. floor += 1; roomIndex 0; currentFloor null; phase floor_start.
- canExtract(run): true only when phase is floor_start AND floor > 1.
- extract(run): THROW unless canExtract. score = scoreRun(run).total; phase extracted; banked = finalScore = score.
- die(run): THROW if ended. FIRST: if run.stats.secondWind is truthy AND run.secondWindUsedFloor !== run.floor: return the run with hp 1, secondWindUsedFloor = floor, phase = (phase was floor_start ? floor_start : "room") — survived. ELSE if run.stats.floorRetry is truthy AND !run.loopUsed: return run with phase floor_start, roomIndex 0, currentFloor null, draft [], loopUsed true, hp = maxHp, held UNCHANGED (The Loop). ELSE: phase dead, banked 0, finalScore = scoreRun(run).total.

Scoring. Import `ITEM_BY_ID` from "core/items.js". Export `STYLE_BONUSES`: an array of at least 5 objects { id, name, points, when } where `when` is a predicate over a run and points > 0; ids unique. It MUST include: id "untouchable" (when roomsCleared > 0 AND hp >= maxHp), id "hoarder" (when held.length >= 10), id "cursed" (when any held id maps to an item whose rarity is "cursed"). Add more of your own (e.g. deep_diver, massacre, minimalist).
Export `scoreRun(run)` returning { total, breakdown } — never mutate run. kills = (run.kills ?? 0) * 10; rooms = (run.roomsCleared ?? 0) * 50; depthMult = 1 + max(0, (run.depthReached ?? 1) - 1) * 0.5 (so depth 1 => exactly 1); bonuses = the STYLE_BONUSES whose `when(run)` is true, each reported as { id, name, points }; bonusTotal = their sum; total = Math.round((kills + rooms + bonusTotal) * depthMult) — an integer. breakdown = { kills, rooms, depthMult, bonuses, bonusTotal }. A fresh run (all zeros, no bonuses) scores 0.

Daily seed and seed codes. Export `dailySeed(date = new Date())`: build the key string `${date.getUTCFullYear()}-${date.getUTCMonth()+1}-${date.getUTCDate()}` (UTC, so the whole world shares one daily) and hash it with 32-bit FNV-1a (offset 2166136261, prime 16777619, `Math.imul`, `>>> 0`) to a non-negative 32-bit integer. Same UTC day => same seed; consecutive days must differ by more than 1000 (it is a hash, not a day count).
Export `formatSeed(seed)`: encode `seed >>> 0` in base 36 using the alphabet "0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ" (uppercase), no padding, at most 8 chars.
Export `parseSeed(text)`: return null unless text is a string; trim and uppercase; empty => null; any char outside [A-Z0-9] => null; otherwise decode base 36 and return `>>> 0`. There is NO decimal special case — "10" decodes to 36. parseSeed(formatSeed(s)) === s for every 32-bit s.

Touch aim assist — pure vector maths. Export `aimAssist(aimDir, targets, strength, opts = {})`. aimDir is a unit vector {x,y,z}; targets is an array of positions {x,y,z} RELATIVE to the shooter (shooter at origin); strength in [0,1]; opts.coneDeg defaults to 8. Return a NEW unit vector; never mutate inputs.
If strength <= 0 or targets is empty: return a copy of aimDir. Otherwise, for each target compute its direction (normalise the position) and the angle between aimDir and that direction via acos(dot). Ignore targets with dot <= 0 (behind the shooter) and targets whose angle exceeds the cone (coneDeg in radians). Among the rest choose the SMALLEST ANGLE (nearest to the aim axis — NOT nearest by distance). If none: return a copy of aimDir. Otherwise return normalise(aimDir + (targetDir - aimDir) * min(1, strength)) — so strength 1 lands exactly on the target direction and 0.5 bends about halfway.

Render quality tiers. Export `TIERS` = { low: { resScale: 0.6, shadows: false, particles: 60 }, medium: { resScale: 0.8, shadows: false, particles: 200 }, high: { resScale: 1.0, shadows: true, particles: 600 } } (you may add more knobs; keep these values and ordering: resScale and particles non-decreasing low→high, shadows false/false/true).
Export `pickQualityTier(benchmarkMs, hints = {})` returning "low"|"medium"|"high". benchmarkMs is how long a fixed startup workload took (lower = faster device). Rules in order: (1) if hints.override is a valid tier name, return it. (2) tier = benchmarkMs <= 8 ? "high" : benchmarkMs <= 25 ? "medium" : "low" — monotone, slower never higher. (3) if hints.mobile is true, cap at medium. (4) if hints.deviceMemory is a number <= 2, cap at low. Missing hints behave like desktop.

Hit resolution and status ticking. Export `resolveHit(shot, target, stats, rng)` and `tickStatuses(target, dt)`. Never mutate arguments; return new objects.

`shot` = { isHeadshot, isFirstShot, isLastShot } booleans. `target` = { hp, maxHp, armor (number, may be absent => 0), statuses: [] }. `stats` = resolved numbers: damage, critChance, critMult (default 2), executeBelow (0 = off), onHitBurn (seconds, 0 = off), onHitSlow (fraction, 0 = off), lifesteal (fraction), firstShotMult, lastShotMult (may be absent => 0).

resolveHit returns { damage, crit, executed, killed, hpAfter, heal, statusesAfter }:
1. dmg = stats.damage. If shot.isFirstShot and stats.firstShotMult: dmg *= (1 + firstShotMult). If shot.isLastShot and stats.lastShotMult: dmg *= (1 + lastShotMult).
2. crit = shot.isHeadshot OR (rng.next() < stats.critChance). critChance 0 never crits, 1 always. If crit, dmg *= critMult.
3. dmg = max(1, dmg - armor).
4. hpAfter = max(0, hp - dmg). Then Executioner: if executeBelow > 0 AND hpAfter > 0 AND hpAfter <= maxHp * executeBelow, set executed = true and hpAfter = 0. Otherwise executed = false.
5. killed = hpAfter <= 0. heal = dmg * (lifesteal ?? 0).
6. statusesAfter: a deep-ish copy of target.statuses (copy each status object), then: if onHitBurn > 0 — if a status with kind "burn" exists, ADD onHitBurn to its duration (one entry only); else push { kind: "burn", duration: onHitBurn, dps: 5 }. If onHitSlow > 0 — if a "slow" exists, set its duration to 2 and its amount to max(existing, onHitSlow); else push { kind: "slow", duration: 2, amount: onHitSlow }.

tickStatuses(target, dt) returns { damage, speedMult, hpAfter, killed, statusesAfter }: for each status (copied): burn deals dps * min(dt, duration) — the last partial tick is capped to remaining duration; slow contributes speedMult = min(speedMult, 1 - amount) (start at 1). Every status's duration decreases by dt; drop any with duration <= 0. hpAfter = max(0, hp - totalDamage). killed = hpAfter <= 0 AND totalDamage > 0. No statuses => damage 0, speedMult 1.

Enemy tables and scaling. Export `ENEMY_ARCHETYPES`: an object with EXACTLY the keys skitter, sentinel, brute, popper, warden, wisp — each { name, hp, speed, damage, role, tell } where role is one of "melee","ranged","suicide","shield","flyer" and tell is a short string. Design intent that tests check: skitter has the LOWEST hp and the HIGHEST speed; brute has the HIGHEST hp and the LOWEST speed. Suggested: skitter hp30 speed9 dmg8 melee; sentinel hp60 speed4 dmg12 ranged; brute hp220 speed3 dmg35 melee; popper hp25 speed8 dmg40 suicide; warden hp140 speed3.5 dmg18 shield; wisp hp40 speed7 dmg15 flyer.
Export `AFFIXES`: an object with EXACTLY these keys, each { name, minFloor }: armoured(1), hasty(1), regenerating(1), explosive(2), shielded(2), splitting(3), vampiric(3).
Export `scaleEnemy(archetype, floor, roomIndex, affix = null)`: throw on unknown archetype. d = max(0, floor-1), room = max(0, roomIndex). Return a NEW object { archetype, name, role, tell, hp, maxHp, damage, speed, armor: 0, affix } where hp = Math.round(base.hp * (1 + d*0.32 + room*0.04)) (so floor 1 room 0 equals base exactly, non-decreasing in both, floor 10 at least 3x floor 1), maxHp = hp, damage = base.damage * (1 + d*0.15 + room*0.03) (floor 1 room 0 equals base), speed = base.speed UNCHANGED by floor/room. If affix is given: set .affix; armoured => armor = 4 + d; hasty => speed = base.speed * 1.4; regenerating => regen field; shielded => shield field. Unknown affix throws.
Export `rollAffix(rng, floor)`: rng.pick from the AFFIXES keys whose minFloor <= floor. So splitting/vampiric never appear on floors 1–2.
Export `rollRoster(rng, floor, roomIndex, mods = {})`: return an array of archetype ids. Count n = rng.int(3 + floor(d*0.6), 6 + floor(d*0.9)) so floor 1 gives 3–6 and deeper floors give more on average. Pick each from a pool: on floor 1 the pool contains only skitter, sentinel, popper, wisp (NO brute, NO warden); from floor 2 add warden and brute. If mods.swarm is true, return the array concatenated with itself (exactly double).

export function rng(seed) — a seeded PRNG. `seed` may be a number or a numeric string; coerce with `Number(seed) >>> 0`. Use the mulberry32 algorithm. Return an object with:
- next(): float in [0, 1)
- int(lo, hi): integer, INCLUSIVE on both ends: `lo + Math.floor(next() * (hi - lo + 1))`
- pick(arr): a uniformly random element
- chance(p): boolean, `next() < p` (so chance(0) is always false, chance(1) always true)
- shuffle(arr): a NEW shuffled copy (Fisher–Yates); must not mutate the input
- fork(label): a NEW independent rng. Its seed must derive ONLY from the ORIGINAL seed and the label (e.g. `rng(originalSeed ^ hash(String(label)))` with a simple 32-bit FNV-1a string hash) — NOT from the parent's current internal state. This means: forking after several draws gives the same stream as forking immediately, and drawing from a fork does not advance the parent. Different labels give different streams.
Every method must be deterministic for a given seed. next() must be roughly uniform (a 20,000-draw histogram into 10 buckets has every bucket between 1,600 and 2,400).

Stat resolution. Export `BASE_STATS` — an object with at least maxHp:100, damage:1, fireRate:1, moveSpeed:8, critChance:0.05, critMult:2, spread:1, and any other numeric baselines you like. Export `computeStats(base, held)` where base is a stats object and held is an array of item objects (each `{ id, stacks, effects }` with effects in the {add}/{mul}/true shape). Return a NEW object (never mutate base):
1. If an item has stacks:false and the same id appears more than once in held, apply it only ONCE. Stacking items apply once per copy.
2. For each stat key: result = (base[key] ?? 0 + sum of all `add`) * (product of all `mul`). Adds are summed FIRST, then multiplied — so base 100 with add 50 and mul 2 gives 300. Stats that appear only in items (not in base) still appear on the result.
3. `true` flag effects set that key to true on the result. Keys no item sets are left as they were in base (or absent).
4. Cap `critChance` at 1.
5. `deflect` uses DIMINISHING stacking: with N copies each of value p, result = 1 - (1 - p)^N (never reaches 1).
6. `maxHp` is never below 1.
Order of items in held must not affect the result.

The reward draft. Import `ITEMS` from "core/items.js". Export `RARITY_WEIGHTS` = { common: 60, uncommon: 28, rare: 10, legendary: 2 } (decreasing). Export `draftRewards(rng, run, n)` returning an array of item objects (the SAME object references from ITEMS). `run` is `{ held: [ids], floor: number, cursesEnabled: boolean, stats: { draftSize, luck, rarityShift } }`; never mutate it. `n` defaults to `run.stats.draftSize` (then 3).
Eligibility — an item may be offered only if ALL hold: (a) it is not already in run.held, UNLESS it has stacks:true; (b) its `requires` is null OR is in run.held; (c) its rarity is not "cursed" UNLESS run.cursesEnabled is true. Never offer the same item twice in one draft. If fewer eligible items exist than n, return fewer.
Rarity: for each pick, choose a tier by weighted random from RARITY_WEIGHTS (plus a weight of 8 for "cursed" only when cursesEnabled), then a uniformly random eligible item of that tier; if that tier has no eligible item left, pick from any tier still available. Deeper floors (run.floor - 1) and higher luck must shift weight toward rarer tiers — multiply each tier's weight by `1 + tierIndex * ((floor - 1) * 0.15 + luck * 1.5)` where tierIndex is 0 for common … 3 for legendary. `rarityShift` (Greed) removes tiers below it: rarityShift 1 means commons are NEVER offered.
On floor 1 with luck 0: commons must be the most frequent, then uncommon, rare, legendary; legendaries must still appear but under 8% of picks. Draw randomness ONLY from the rng argument.

Weapons. Export `ARCHETYPES`: an object with EXACTLY these six keys and these numbers — sidearm {name, damage:12, fireRate:5, magSize:12, spread:1, reloadTime, projSpeed, pellets:1}; scattergun {damage:9, fireRate:1.2, magSize:6, spread:8, pellets:8, ...}; carbine {damage:18, fireRate:8, magSize:30, spread:2, pellets:1}; railgun {damage:90, fireRate:0.7, magSize:3, spread:0, pellets:1, pierce:99, critMult:3}; launcher {damage:60, fireRate:1, magSize:4, splashRadius:3, selfDamage:0.5, arcs:true, pellets:1}; beam {damage:30, fireRate:10, magSize:1, spread:0, continuous:true, rampTo:90, rampTime:2, heatCap:4, pellets:1}. Every archetype has numeric name-less fields damage, fireRate, magSize, spread, reloadTime, projSpeed and a string `name`.
Export `WEAPON_MODS`: an object of AT LEAST 15 mods keyed by id, each `{ name, effects }` with effects in the {add}/{mul}/true shape. It MUST include these ids: ricochet {ricochet:true}, pierce {pierce:{add:1}}, incendiary, cryo, chain_lightning, lifesteal, big_mag {magSize:{mul:1.5}}, fast_reload {reloadTime:{mul:0.6}}, crit_chance {critChance:{add:0.15}}, crit_damage {critMult:{add:0.5}}, tight_spread {spread:{mul:0.5}}. Add more of your own to reach 15+.
Export `applyMods(stats, modIds)`: return a NEW stats object with every mod's effects applied — sum all `add`s then multiply by all `mul`s per key, `true` sets a flag; unknown mod id throws. AFTER applying, if `magSize` is a number, round it to the nearest whole number with `Math.round` and clamp to at least 1. Empty modIds returns an equal copy.
Export `rollWeapon(rng, archetype, floor)`: throw on unknown archetype. Pick rarity from [common, uncommon, rare, legendary] with weights [60, 28 + d*4, 10 + d*3, 2 + d] where d = max(0, floor-1) (so deeper floors roll rarer). Build `baseStats` = a copy of the archetype (without `name`) where each of damage, fireRate, magSize, spread, reloadTime, projSpeed that is a non-zero number is multiplied by a jitter in [0.9, 1.1] drawn from rng; then round baseStats.magSize to a whole number ≥ 1. Choose a mod COUNT by rarity: common exactly 1, uncommon 1–2, rare 2–3, legendary exactly 3 (use rng.int). Choose that many DISTINCT mod ids (rng.shuffle the keys and slice). Return `{ archetype, rarity, mods, baseStats, stats: applyMods(baseStats, mods) }`. Deterministic for a given rng seed.

Floor generation. Export `ROOM_MODIFIERS`: an object with keys low_gravity, darkness, swarm, no_dash, time_pressure, each `{ name, desc }`. Export `HAZARD_TAGS`: an array of at least 4 strings (e.g. lava_floor, turrets, mines, acid_pools, collapsing). Export `BOSSES`: an object with EXACTLY the keys custodian, chorus, landlord, each `{ name, hp }` (hp a number).
Export `generateFloor(rng, floorIndex, run)` — never mutate run. Return `{ index: floorIndex, rooms, boss }` where rooms is an array of EXACTLY 5 room objects `{ index (0..4), modifier, hazardTag, eliteCount, rewardType, doors }`:
- modifier: null or a key of ROOM_MODIFIERS. Probability of a modifier is `min(0.15 + d*0.07, 0.6)` where d = max(0, floorIndex-1) — so some rooms have none, and deeper floors have more. Room index 0 must NEVER have modifier no_dash or time_pressure (if rolled, set it to null).
- hazardTag: null or an element of HAZARD_TAGS.
- eliteCount: integer ≥ 0. On floorIndex 1 it is 0 or 1 only. Deeper floors allow more (up to 4) and average more.
- rewardType: one of "item", "weapon", "heal", "shop", "curse" — weighted toward item.
- doors: for rooms 0–3, an array of 2 or 3 door objects `{ leadsTo: index+1, preview: { rewardType, hazardTag, hasElite } }` where the preview fields are copied EXACTLY from the NEXT room (rooms[index+1]) — hasElite is `next.eliteCount > 0`. Room 4 has exactly ONE door `{ leadsTo: "boss", preview: null }`.
boss: `{ id (a key of BOSSES), name (BOSSES[id].name), affix (a string from a list of at least 4, e.g. armoured, hasty, regenerating, explosive, shielded), hp: Math.round(BOSSES[id].hp * (1 + d*0.35)) }` so hp grows with floor. All randomness from rng; deterministic per seed.

A combat pacing director. It decides HOW an encounter is fed to the player: not one
wall of enemies, but waves that arrive as the room is fought, tuned to how well the player
is doing. No `three`, no DOM.

Export `DIFFICULTY_BANDS`: an array of at least 3 objects `{ name, max }`, ordered by
ascending `max`, describing skill bands from worst to best. `max` values are the INCLUSIVE
upper bound of the band, strictly increasing, and the LAST one must be exactly 1.
Example shape: `[{name:"struggling",max:0.3},{name:"steady",max:0.7},{name:"dominant",max:1}]`.

Export `planEncounter(rng, { floor, roomIndex, roster, skill })`.
`roster` is an array of enemy archetype id strings (may repeat, may be empty). `skill` is a
number that SHOULD be 0..1 but may be junk (negative, >1, NaN) — clamp it to 0..1, treating
a non-finite value as 0.5. Never mutate `roster`.
Return `{ band, waves }` where:
- `band` is the `name` of the first entry of DIFFICULTY_BANDS whose `max` is >= the clamped
  skill (fall back to the last band).
- `waves` is an array of `{ delay, ids }`. Every element of `roster` appears in exactly one
  wave, and nothing else appears — the union of all `ids` is a permutation of `roster`.
  `ids` is never empty. `delay` is seconds from the start of the room, a finite number >= 0.
  The FIRST wave always has `delay` exactly 0. Delays are non-decreasing across the array.
- An empty roster returns `{ band, waves: [] }`.
- A one-element roster returns exactly one wave containing it.
- On `floor` 1 and `roomIndex` 0 — the player's very first room — the first wave must contain
  at most `Math.ceil(roster.length / 2)` enemies, so the game does not open with a wall.
- A HIGHER skill means the later waves arrive SOONER (the player is being pushed): the delay
  of the last wave must be smaller on average for skill 0.95 than for skill 0.05. Make this a
  clear multiplier on the gap between waves, not a subtle one.
- Deterministic: same rng seed and inputs => identical result. Different seeds must give
  different plans (vary wave sizes and the exact gaps with the rng).

Export `updateSkill(prev, perf)` where `perf` is `{ clearedSecs, damageTaken, accuracy }` and
any field may be missing. Return a NEW number in 0..1 — an exponential moving average that
nudges `prev` toward a score computed from the room: fast clear, little damage taken and high
accuracy push it up; slow, bloody, inaccurate pushes it down. Never mutate `perf`. A single
room must never move the value by more than 0.25, so one unlucky room does not reclassify the
player. Non-finite or missing fields are treated as average, and the result is always finite.

LENGTH IS CRITICAL: the whole module must be UNDER 110 LINES. A previous attempt ran past the
output limit and was cut off mid-file, so it would not even parse. Write it tight: short
helper functions, no long comment blocks, no defensive branches you do not need. Finish the
file.

WAVES MUST ACTUALLY BE WAVES. A previous attempt put the entire roster into a single wave with
delay 0, which passes "every enemy appears once" but defeats the whole purpose. Rules:
- A roster of 4 or more enemies MUST be split into at least 2 waves, and the last wave's delay
  must be greater than 0. Aim for 2-4 waves depending on roster size.
- A roster of 2 or 3 may be one or two waves; only a 1-enemy roster is always a single wave.
- Because the last wave's delay must be > 0 and must shrink as skill rises, compute gaps like
  `baseGap * (1.6 - 1.1 * skill)` — at skill 0 the gaps are long, at skill 1 they are short,
  but they are never zero.

Optional per-room challenges: a small objective offered alongside a room, e.g. "clear it
without reloading". Pure data + predicates, no `three`, no DOM.

A `stats` object describes what the player did in a room. Its fields (all numbers, ANY of
which may be missing — treat a missing field as 0):
`kills, headshots, damageTaken, reloads, secs, dashes, shotsFired, shotsHit, itemsTaken`.

Export `CHALLENGES`: an object of at least 8 entries keyed by id. Each entry is
`{ id, name, desc, minFloor, reward, rewardAmount, test, progress }` where:
- `id` equals its own key. `name` is short and unique across the table. `desc` is one line
  telling the player exactly what to do.
- `minFloor` is an integer >= 1 — the earliest floor this may be offered on.
- `reward` is one of "gold", "item", "heal", "reroll". `rewardAmount` is a number > 0.
- `test(stats)` returns a boolean: was the challenge met?
- `progress(stats)` returns a number 0..1: how close the player is. It MUST return exactly 1
  whenever `test(stats)` is true.
Every challenge must be discriminating: it is FALSE for an all-zero stats object and TRUE for
a heroic one (`{kills:40, headshots:30, damageTaken:0, reloads:0, secs:12, dashes:25,
shotsFired:40, shotsHit:40, itemsTaken:0}`), or vice versa. A challenge that gives the same
verdict for both is a bug — for example "take no damage" would be true for BOTH, so phrase it
as something that also requires action, like "clear the room without taking damage" (which
needs kills > 0 too). Ideas: enough headshots, no reloads while still killing, clear under N
seconds, a minimum accuracy, kill N with dashes used, kill N without taking damage.

Export `rollChallenge(rng, floor, exclude = [])` — pick one challenge at random from those
whose `minFloor <= floor` and whose id is not in `exclude`. Return the challenge object, or
`null` if nothing qualifies. Deterministic for a given seed.

Export `checkChallenge(challenge, stats)` — returns `challenge.test(stats)` as a boolean, never
throwing on missing fields, never mutating `stats`.

Export `challengeProgress(challenge, stats)` — returns `{ frac, text }` where `frac` is the
challenge's `progress(stats)` clamped to 0..1 and `text` is a short human string such as
`"3 / 5 headshots"`. Never mutates `stats`.

TWO THINGS THAT ARE EASY TO GET WRONG:
- `progress` must return exactly 1 whenever `test` is true, INCLUDING for challenges where
  lower is better. For "clear the room in under N seconds", progress is NOT `secs / N` — that
  reads 0.4 when the player finished in 12 of 30 seconds and has actually SUCCEEDED. Compute
  such a challenge's progress so that meeting it gives 1, e.g. `test(stats) ? 1 : clamped
  partial credit`. Check every entry: if `test(stats)` is true then `progress(stats) === 1`.
- The heroic reference room is `{kills:40, headshots:30, damageTaken:0, reloads:0, secs:12,
  dashes:25, shotsFired:40, shotsHit:40, itemsTaken:4}` and the lazy one is all zeros. Every
  challenge you write must come out TRUE for one of those two and FALSE for the other. Do not
  write a challenge that is false for both (e.g. one needing a stat that is 0 in both).

Persistent meta-progression across runs: totals and unlocks. Pure functions over a plain
profile object. No `three`, no DOM, no localStorage — the caller does the storing.

A `runSummary` is `{ floorsCleared, roomsCleared, kills, bossesKilled, extracted, score,
itemsHeld, secs }`. Any field may be missing; treat missing numbers as 0, missing `extracted`
as false, missing `itemsHeld` as [].

Export `UNLOCKS`: an object of at least 10 entries keyed by id. Each is
`{ id, name, desc, kind, requires }` where `id` equals its key, `name` is short and unique,
`desc` is one line, `kind` is one of "weapon" | "item" | "cosmetic" | "modifier" | "start",
and `requires` is a NON-EMPTY object of threshold conditions checked against a profile's
running totals, e.g. `{ kills: 500 }`, `{ bestScore: 5000 }`, `{ bossesKilled: 1 }`,
`{ runs: 10 }`, `{ deepestFloor: 3 }`, `{ extractions: 3 }`.
Tune the thresholds so that at least one unlock is earned by a first competent run
(5 rooms, 1 floor, 40 kills, score 500) and several require far more.

Export `newProfile()` — a fresh object `{ version: 1, unlocked: [], totals: { runs: 0,
kills: 0, bestScore: 0, ... } }`. `totals` must include every key any `requires` mentions,
all starting at 0. Return a NEW object each call (no shared state).

Export `applyRun(profile, runSummary)` — returns `{ profile, newlyUnlocked }` WITHOUT mutating
the input. `profile.totals.runs` increments by 1, cumulative totals add, `bestScore` becomes
the max of the old value and this run's score, `deepestFloor` the max floor reached.
`newlyUnlocked` is an array of ids that became satisfied on THIS call — never already-owned
ids, never duplicates. Those ids are appended to `profile.unlocked`, which never shrinks and
never contains duplicates. A run summary of all zeros unlocks nothing. A `{}` summary must not
throw and must still count as one run.

Export `isUnlocked(profile, id)` — boolean, false for unknown ids, never throws.

Export `serializeProfile(profile)` — returns a string (JSON is fine).
Export `deserializeProfile(text)` — parses it back. On ANY failure (empty string, undefined,
malformed JSON, `"null"`, an array, wrong field types) return a fresh `newProfile()` instead
of throwing. Ids in `unlocked` that are not keys of `UNLOCKS` are dropped — an old save must
not carry ghosts from a previous build. Missing totals are filled in from `newProfile()`.
A valid profile round-trips exactly: `deserializeProfile(serializeProfile(p))` deep-equals `p`.

Export `profileSummary(profile)` — returns `{ unlockedCount, totalCount, text }` where
`totalCount` is the number of entries in UNLOCKS and `text` is a short human line.

Boss attack choreography: which attack a boss uses next, and the tell that precedes it.
Pure data + selection. No `three`, no DOM.

Export `ATTACK_SHAPES`: an object of at least 4 entries keyed by id, each
`{ id, kind, telegraph, windup, duration }` where `id` equals its key, `kind` is one of
"ranged" | "melee" | "area" | "summon", `telegraph` is a short (<= 40 characters) line
describing the visible tell, and `windup` and `duration` are numbers > 0 in seconds. Every
attack has a wind-up: the player must always be able to see it coming.
Suggested shapes: sweep_beam, shockwave, mortar_volley, summon_adds, charge_slam, spore_cloud.

Export `BOSS_PATTERNS`: an object with EXACTLY the keys `custodian`, `chorus`, `landlord`.
Each is `{ phases }` — an array of EXACTLY 3 entries, each `{ attacks, cooldown }`:
- `attacks` is an array of at least 2 ATTACK_SHAPES ids (all must exist in ATTACK_SHAPES).
- `cooldown` is seconds between attacks, a number > 0.
- Phases escalate: `phases[1].cooldown <= phases[0].cooldown`,
  `phases[2].cooldown <= phases[1].cooldown`, and `phases[2].cooldown < phases[0].cooldown`.
- The three bosses must not have identical attack line-ups — give each its own character.

Export `bossPhase(hpFrac)` — maps remaining-health fraction to phase index 0, 1 or 2.
Full health is phase 0 and a sliver is phase 2; the result never decreases as hp drops.
Clamp junk: `bossPhase(5)` is 0, `bossPhase(-5)` is 2, `bossPhase(NaN)` returns some valid
phase index without throwing.

Export `nextAttack(rng, bossId, hpFrac, prevShape)` — throws an Error naming the boss if
`bossId` is not in BOSS_PATTERNS. Otherwise picks one shape from the CURRENT phase's `attacks`
and returns `{ shape, phase, kind, telegraph, windup, duration, cooldown }`, where `phase` is
`bossPhase(hpFrac)` and `cooldown` comes from that phase (you may vary it slightly with the
rng, but a later phase must still be faster on average than phase 0). The chosen `shape` must
never equal `prevShape` when the phase offers any alternative — bosses do not repeat
themselves back to back. If `prevShape` is not in this phase's list (or is null), any shape is
fine. Deterministic for a given rng seed.

Export `telegraphFor(shapeId)` — returns the shape's `telegraph`, or a generic short string
for an unknown id. Never throws, always returns a string of at most 40 characters.

Deterministic set dressing for arena rooms: where the crates, pipes, terminals and hanging
cables go. Pure layout only — no `three`, no DOM, no rendering. The game turns your data into
meshes.

An `arena` is `{ halfW, halfD, blocks }`. `blocks` is an array of cover boxes
`{ x, z, w, d }` centred at (x, z). The room spans x in [-halfW, halfW] and z in
[-halfD, halfD]. The player spawns at (0, halfD - 4) and must not be blocked in.

Export `PROP_KINDS`: an object of AT LEAST 6 entries keyed by id, each
`{ id, mount, w, h, d, emissive, maxPerRoom }` where:
- `id` equals its own key.
- `mount` is "floor" | "wall" | "ceiling" — where the prop attaches.
- `w`, `h`, `d` are its size in metres, all > 0. Keep them plausible: a crate is about
  0.8 x 0.8 x 0.8, a pipe run is long and thin, a wall terminal is flat.
- `emissive` is a boolean — does it glow (a screen, a strip light) or not (a crate)?
- `maxPerRoom` is an integer > 0: the most of this kind allowed in one room.
Suggested kinds: crate, barrel, pipe_run, wall_terminal, strip_light, hanging_cable,
floor_grate, debris_pile.

Export `layoutDressing(rng, arena, floor)` — returns an ARRAY of placed props, each
`{ kind, x, y, z, rotY, scale }`, all five numeric fields finite and `scale` > 0.
`kind` must be a key of PROP_KINDS. Never mutate `arena`.

Placement rules, all enforced by tests:
- Return between 6 and 80 props. Never zero — an empty room reads unfinished.
- Never exceed a kind's `maxPerRoom`.
- FLOOR props: keep `x` within [-halfW, halfW] and `z` within [-halfD, halfD]; never place one
  INSIDE a cover block (that is, not both `|x - b.x| < b.w/2` and `|z - b.z| < b.d/2`); and
  never within 2.5 metres of the spawn point (0, halfD - 4). If a random position violates any
  of these, resample — but cap the number of attempts (e.g. 12) and simply skip that prop if
  you cannot place it, so a tiny or crowded arena can never loop forever.
- WALL props: must sit near a wall — either `| |x| - halfW | < 1.5` or `| |z| - halfD | < 1.5`.
  Give them a `rotY` that would face into the room.
- CEILING props: put `y` up high (3 or more).
- `y` for floor props is normally 0 or half the prop height; use your judgement.
- Deeper floors may be dressed differently but must not be dressed LESS: the total prop count
  for floor 5 must be at least 80% of the count for floor 1, averaged over seeds.
- Deterministic: the same rng seed and arena give an identical array. Different seeds differ.

A tiny arena `{ halfW: 6, halfD: 6, blocks: [] }` must still return a non-empty array.

Keep the whole module UNDER 130 LINES and finish it — a file that runs past the output limit
is cut off and cannot be parsed.
